prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The SNP’s 1997 manifesto argues Scotland can and should become independent to use its wealth for jobs, public services and social justice. It claims Scotland has been a net contributor to the UK, would be among the world’s richer nations with its North Sea share, and would retain EU membership, open borders with England, and secure pensions and investments.

Route to independence: win a majority of Scottish seats at a UK General Election, open talks with the UK and EU, then hold a single-question referendum on the negotiated settlement. On approval, declare independence and hold new elections.

Constitution and governance: adopt a written constitution and Bill of Rights; a single-chamber parliament elected by proportional representation; votes from age 16; public petition powers; strong committees instead of a House of Lords; reform the monarchy’s role and funding; entrench local government and elect councils by PR; guaranteed residency and citizenship by birth or residence.

Economy and tax: aim for full employment and create 100,000 jobs via independence-led growth, apprenticeships, exports and R&D. Propose a competitive business-tax package: reduce corporation tax (main rate to 30p; small firms to 18p), cap business-rate increases, band rates to help smaller firms, abolish Class IV NICs. Personal tax: introduce a 15p starter rate, widen the basic-rate band, remove the NI ceiling for high earners; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5% and seek further relief. Back tourism, fair trading, late-payment controls, and adopt the EU Social Chapter with a negotiated minimum wage.

Social justice and health: raise Child Benefit to £12.50; restore benefits for 16–17 year-olds; a pensioners’ package (pension rises, cold-climate allowance, remove utility standing charges, end means-testing for residential care). Rebuild a true NHS by abolishing the internal market, integrating services, adding £35m per year and cutting bureaucracy; reintegrate dentistry; reform prescription charges; ban tobacco advertising and raise tobacco duty; strengthen care in the community and disability rights; establish a Scottish Food and Consumer Health Agency.

Crime and justice: support “zero tolerance” for community crime, add police resources, expand alternatives to prison, invest in rehabilitation research, and ban handguns with Cullen recommendations implemented.

Education and housing: hire 700 teachers, repair schools, guarantee free nursery education for 3–4 year-olds, restore student grants, expand training, and bring technology to classrooms; support Gaelic, Scots and community language needs. Tackle housing by transferring 75% of council housing debt to central government, building and renovating social homes, ending homelessness, protecting new stock from discounted right-to-buy, and replacing Scottish Homes with an accountable agency.

Land, rural economy and environment: abolish feudal tenure; create a Land Commission and a public land register; transfer Crown Estate coastal powers locally. Agriculture: BSE traceability, CAP reform, diversification, producer access to markets. Forestry: double woodland cover in 25 years, prioritize native species. Fisheries: regional control, support processing and research. Strengthen SEPA, set national environmental targets, end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay and pivot to renewables and decommissioning.

Energy and transport: secure Scotland’s North Sea share on established legal lines; honour existing oil/gas obligations; tackle discriminatory gas pricing; phase out nuclear power while investing in renewables and efficiency; reassess coal. Build an integrated transport system: bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership, electrify key routes, integrate buses, remove bridge tolls (starting with Skye), support ferries, adjust Air Passenger Duty for remote areas, and expand direct air links. Promote telecoms competition and rural connectivity; champion internet adoption for schools, homes and business.

Europe, world and defence: full EU membership with votes, more MEPs, a Scottish Commissioner and turn at the EU Presidency; targeted diplomatic network; join the UN, Council of Europe and Commonwealth; foster a British Isles association. Establish Scottish Defence Forces (army, navy, air force), withdraw Trident, pursue a phased exit from NATO’s nuclear alliance while engaging in European and partnership structures; create a peacekeeping college; support defence diversification and use Rosyth for refit.

Paying for it: a four-year, fully costed plan reallocates spending (including from Trident), uses an expected fiscal surplus relative to the UK, models growth-driven revenues and savings, and commits £6.6bn to national debt reduction over four years, funding enterprise, social justice, education, health and infrastructure. The core message: “Yes We Can” deliver a fair, prosperous, independent Scotland.
